stem: The positive number \(a\) is \(40\%\) greater than the positive number \(b\), and the positive number \(c\) is \(30\%\) less than \(b\). The number \(a\) is what percent greater than \(c\)?
solution: \(\frac{a}{c} = \frac{1.4b}{0.7b} = 2\), so \(a\) is twice \(c\), which is \(100\%\) greater than \(c\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(40\% - 30\%\). The percents are measured from \(b\), not from \(c\), so they cannot be subtracted to compare \(a\) with \(c\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(40\% + 30\%\). Adding the two percents ignores that \(c\) is a smaller base than \(b\).
explanation.C: Correct. \(a = 2c\), so \(a\) exceeds \(c\) by \(c\), which is \(100\%\) of \(c\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. The number \(a\) is \(200\%\) of \(c\), but it is only \(100\%\) greater than \(c\): the amount by which \(a\) exceeds \(c\) is \(a - c = c\).

verify:
b = symbols('b', positive=True)
a, c = Rational(14, 10)*b, Rational(7, 10)*b
ans = simplify((a - c)/c)
assert ans == 1
assert value(choices[answer]) == ans
assert all(value(choices[k]) != ans for k in choices if k != answer)
